The frontal and insular location is also highly characteristic of IDH-mutant tumors. The involvement of the insula ('Region Proportions') and deep gray matter structures ('Anatomical Overlap Regions' including caudate and putamen) are strong indicators of an astrocytic lineage. Furthermore, the presence of 'Deep WM invasion' suggests an infiltrative pattern more typical of astrocytoma. While frontal and cortical involvement can be seen in oligodendroglioma, the combination of insular and deep structural involvement makes non-codeletion much more likely.

overall_comment: The imaging features are highly characteristic of an IDH-mutant astrocytoma. The patient's young age and the large, non-enhancing, infiltrative nature of the tumor in the frontal and insular lobes strongly support this molecular subtype. While the distinction between WHO grade 2 and 3 is challenging on imaging alone, the substantial tumor volume and mass effect favor a grade 3 designation. The integrated diagnosis is Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 3.
